minSize.source: ADR-0014 (integrator decision 2026-10-22, the macOS model: small icons stay legible): icon edge in logical pixels below which the icon appearance modes do not apply and the Default artwork is drawn in every mode (list rows, menus, the sidebar: a plate and a recolour made json, cpp, txt, sh and csv the same tile at 16 px)

sysPlateInset.source: ADR-0014 Dark/Clear/Tinted: the system plate every icon sits on is inset by this fraction of the icon box on each side (macOS 26 plates leave a small margin)

sysPlateRadius.source: ADR-0014 Dark/Clear/Tinted: corner radius of the system plate over its side (macOS squircle proportion, about 22.5 percent)

sysGlyphScale.source: ADR-0014 Dark/Clear/Tinted: scale of the artwork of every icon sitting on the system plate (macOS 26 shrinks artwork into the plate)

ownTileAlpha.source: ADR-0014 own-tile rule: alpha from which a pixel is part of an icon's shape (a shadow or a soft glow is below it and never counts)

ownTileProbeSize.source: ADR-0014 own-tile rule: edge in pixels the icon file is drawn at for the shape test (one read per icon file; an edge is measured to about 1 percent)

ownTileSquare.source: ADR-0014 own-tile rule: largest difference between the width and the height of the shape (over the larger) for it to count as square

ownTileCentre.source: ADR-0014 own-tile rule: largest offset of the centre of the shape from the centre of the box (box fraction)

ownTileMinSide.source: ADR-0014 own-tile rule: smallest edge of the shape over the box for it to be a tile (a smaller square is a glyph and sits on the system plate)

ownTileFillMin.source: ADR-0014 own-tile rule: lowest fill of the shape's box by opaque pixels (a rounded square of radius 22.5 percent fills 0.957, a squircle 0.95, a circle 0.785; 0.9 allows a tile with a badge over one corner)

ownTileFillMax.source: ADR-0014 own-tile rule: highest fill (a square with sharp corners fills 1; the plate's corners are rounded, so such an icon is not a tile)

ownTileProbe.source: ADR-0014 own-tile rule: how far inside the box of the shape (fraction of its edge) the four corners are tested empty and the four edge middles filled

ownTileEdge.source: ADR-0014 own-tile rule: share of the middle half of each of the four edges of the shape that is filled (a folder's tab or a glyph's arms leave gaps, a tile's edge is straight)

ownTileCornersEmpty.source: ADR-0014 own-tile rule: corners of the shape (of four) that must be empty: a tile with a badge over one corner (an emblem sticking out of a tile) is still a tile; a square with sharp corners has none empty

ownTileScaleMin.source: ADR-0014 own-tile rule: lowest artwork scale of a tile icon (its tile is scaled onto the system plate: plate side over tile side)

ownTileScaleMax.source: ADR-0014 own-tile rule: highest artwork scale of a tile icon

ownTileConcurrency.source: estimate: icon files read at once for the shape test [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Settings; docs/specs/settings.md]

ownTileTimeout.source: estimate: ms after which a shape read that did not finish is given up (the icon then sits on the system plate like a glyph) [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Settings; docs/specs/settings.md]

tileDarkArtLift.source: ADR-0014 own-tile rule, Dark: lightness the darkest part of the artwork of a tile icon is mapped to (no lift: the tile covers the plate, so nothing has to separate from it, and a lift flattens the glyph-vs-tile contrast of the icon; A2 rule I)

clearPlateWallpaperLuma.source: ADR-0014 Clear over the bare wallpaper: lightness of the smoked plate (almost black, so a black folder on a black wallpaper still shows its plate while white ink and the plate hold on a white one; a lighter plate costs A2 rule E on mid-green wallpapers, modelled)

prewarmGapMs.source: PERF-01 / UX-13: ms between two shape reads of the prewarm (IconShapePrewarm), one icon file at a time in the idle moments after the list of apps is known, so the Apps panel does not read about a hundred files while it opens [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Settings; docs/specs/settings.md]

tileTintedPlateScaleLight.source: ADR-0014 own-tile rule, Tinted in the light appearance: the plate under a tile icon (seen only in the antialiased fringe of the tile's edge) is the tint at this fraction of its brightness, dark, so that the edge keeps its contrast against a light material (A2 rule E, 32 px)

tileClearPlateAlphaLight.source: ADR-0014 own-tile rule, Clear in the light appearance: opacity of the plate under a tile icon (seen only in the fringe of its edge)

tileClearPlateLightLuma.source: ADR-0014 own-tile rule, Clear in the light appearance: lightness of the plate under a tile icon (black: the fringe of the edge keeps its contrast against a light material)

clearPlateLightLuma.source: ADR-0014 Clear in the light appearance: lightness of the smoked plate (dark grey rather than black, so that a black folder on a black background still shows its plate at the same faint level as over the bare wallpaper; white and bright materials see it as the smoke it is: A2 changes by under 0.1 on every cell, modelled)

clearPlateAlphaWallpaper.source: ADR-0014 Clear over the bare wallpaper (desktop icons): opacity of the smoked glass plate, strong so that white ink and the plate edge hold on a white and on a black wallpaper

darkPlateLuma.source: ADR-0014 Dark: lightness (sRGB 0..1) of the graphite system plate; macOS 26 Dark plates are near black.

darkArtSaturation.source: ADR-0014 Dark: the artwork keeps this share of its colour (1 = unchanged, 0 = grey): a modest desaturation, colour identity kept

darkArtScale.source: ADR-0014 Dark: lightness the lightest part of the artwork is mapped to (a modest darkening; the map is affine from darkArtLift, so it is monotonic and keeps the internal contrast of the icon)

darkArtLift.source: ADR-0014 Dark: lightness the darkest part of the artwork is mapped to (a black part separates a little from the graphite plate; the affine map to darkArtScale keeps black art darker than light art: >= 3:1 where the default has it)

clearPlateAlphaDark.source: ADR-0014 Clear: opacity of the white glass plate in the dark appearance (the material shows through)

clearPlateAlphaLight.source: ADR-0014 Clear: opacity of the dark glass plate in the light appearance (the material shows through)

clearInkDark.source: ADR-0014 Clear: luma of the glyph in the dark appearance (near white)

clearInkLight.source: ADR-0014 Clear: luma of the glyph in the light appearance (near black)

clearBackdropDark.source: ADR-0014 Clear: lightness of the dark window material the glass sits on (the ink opacity is solved so that the composite is affine in linear light between the glass and the ink: the internal contrast of the artwork survives)

clearBackdropLight.source: ADR-0014 Clear: lightness of the light window material the smoked glass sits on

clearBackdropMid.source: ADR-0014 Clear: lightness assumed behind the glass over the bare wallpaper and over an accent fill

clearInkFloor.source: ADR-0014 Clear: share of the ink (in linear light, between the glass and the ink) that even black artwork gets, so that a dark monochrome glyph (Breeze network-wired, fcitx: 1.2:1 on a dark panel) stays distinguishable from the glass: about 2:1 against the plate; part of the black-vs-white internal contrast is traded for it

clearPlateAlphaAccent.source: ADR-0014 Clear over the accent fill of a selected row (Search, Force Quit): opacity of the plate, dark on a bright accent and light on a dark one, so that the plate and the ink keep 4.5:1 against the accent (A2 accent row)

tintedPlateScale.source: ADR-0014 Tinted, dark appearance: the plate is the tint colour at this fraction of its brightness (a dark tinted plate, macOS 26)

tintedPlateMixLight.source: ADR-0014 Tinted, light appearance: the plate is the tint colour mixed this far to white (a light tinted plate)

tintedRampLowDark.source: ADR-0014 Tinted, dark appearance: the artwork's darkest tone is the tint at this fraction of its brightness

tintedRampHighDark.source: ADR-0014 Tinted, dark appearance: the artwork's lightest tone is the tint mixed this far to white

tintedRampLowLight.source: ADR-0014 Tinted, light appearance: the artwork's darkest tone is the tint at this fraction of its brightness (dark on the light plate)

tintedRampHighLight.source: ADR-0014 Tinted, light appearance: the artwork's lightest tone is the tint mixed this far to white (a wide ramp keeps the internal contrast of the icon)

wallpaperLikeTransparency.source: ADR-0014 Clear: from this material transparency (Control Center slider, 0..1) the wallpaper shows through the window material so much that Clear icons are drawn as over the bare wallpaper (smoked plate, opaque rim); A2 at 1.0 holds a floor of 2.0 in every mode, tint and size (docs/specs/ui.md)

previewSize.source: estimate: Settings icon mode picker, sample icon edge (macOS 26 style tiles) [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Settings; docs/specs/settings.md]

previewTileWidth.source: estimate: Settings icon mode picker, tile width [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Settings; docs/specs/settings.md]

previewTileHeight.source: estimate: Settings icon mode picker, tile height [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Settings; docs/specs/settings.md]

previewRadius.source: estimate: Settings icon mode picker, tile corner radius [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Settings; docs/specs/settings.md]

previewGap.source: estimate: Settings icon mode picker, gap between tiles [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Settings; docs/specs/settings.md]

previewFocusGap.source: estimate: Settings icon mode picker, gap between a tile and its keyboard focus ring (the selection ring is the tile border, so the two stay distinct) [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Settings; docs/specs/settings.md]

sampleTop.source: own pick: the blue of the Theme folder colour swatch (Settings and Files Customize Folder); the same blue as the top of the sample icon plate [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Settings; docs/specs/settings.md]

tintColors.source: own picks, not copied: swatches of the Tinted icon colour (blue, purple, pink, red, orange, yellow, green, graphite); the accent is the first swatch [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Settings; docs/specs/settings.md]

saturation.source: folder colours: MultiEffect saturation (0: the colorization alone sets the hue; MultiEffect desaturates after colorizing) [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Files; docs/specs/files.md]

brightness.source: folder colours: lifts the shading so the recoloured body keeps the lightness of the theme's folder (tuned on the former base theme's folders, re-checked on the Breeze folder in the nested session 2026-10-21: symbols 96/96 and 288/288 cells at 3:1, docs/specs/files.md)

contrast.source: folder colours: keeps the flap and the body distinct after the colour mapping (tuned on the former base theme's folders, re-checked on the Breeze folder: flap and body stay distinct) [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Files; docs/specs/files.md]

colorization.source: folder colours: strength of the colour (0..1): the luminance of the folder is mapped onto the colour, shape and shading kept [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Files; docs/specs/files.md]

glyphScale.source: estimate (macOS 26 Customize Folder): symbol or emoji edge over the folder icon edge [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Files; docs/specs/files.md]

glyphCenterY.source: estimate: vertical centre of the symbol over the icon height (the body of the folder, below the flap) [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Files; docs/specs/files.md]

glyphMinContrast.source: A2 (icons >= 3:1): a plain symbol is an engraved shade of the folder's own colour (macOS 26), darkened in the colour's hue until it reaches this contrast against the plate [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Files; docs/specs/files.md]

glyphContrastMargin.source: measured safety over the minimum (the plate is estimated from the colour, the real one differs by a few percent) [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Files; docs/specs/files.md]

plateDefault.source: estimate, only used when the plate cannot be measured (FolderPlate): plate over the folder colour (measured on the fallback theme, tests/visual/folder_glyph_contrast.py), icon mode default and clear [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Files]

themePlate.source: estimate, only used when the plate cannot be measured (FolderPlate): plate of the base icon theme folder (Breeze, flat #3daee9 under the symbol) in default mode; the symbol shade otherwise follows the measured plate, any theme [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Files; docs/specs/files.md]

glyphLighterBelow.source: A2 design rule: in the Tinted icon mode the symbol is engraved lighter when the mode's own folder plate (the theme's folder through the mode) has a relative luminance below this (a lighter shade reaches 3.3:1 on plates up to about 0.268), darker otherwise; Default, Dark and Clear darker (a Dark folder keeps its colour on the dark system plate) [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Files; docs/specs/files.md]

plateSamples.source: estimate: samples per axis of the grid read under the symbol from the raw icon (the plate of every colour, mode and appearance is computed from them) [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Files; docs/specs/files.md]

plateBuckets.source: estimate: icon size buckets of the plate measure (one measure per icon file and bucket); a larger icon uses the last [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Files; docs/specs/files.md]

plateBackdropDark.source: estimate: the view behind a translucent (Clear mode) icon in dark appearance, composited under the plate when its shade is chosen; warm since the owner's warm neutrals of 2026-10-30 (ADR-0040): #1E1F24 at OKLCH hue 85, chroma 0.0075, its lightness kept, so its contrasts stay [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Files; docs/specs/files.md]

plateBackdropLight.source: estimate: the view behind a translucent (Clear mode) icon in light appearance; warm since the owner's warm neutrals of 2026-10-30 (ADR-0040): #F4F5F7 at OKLCH hue 85, chroma 0.0075, its lightness kept, so its contrasts stay [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Files; docs/specs/files.md]

glyphHighlight.source: estimate: 1 px light edge under an engraved symbol (the engraved look) [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Files; docs/specs/files.md]

glyphHighlightOffset.source: estimate: offset of that edge over the icon edge (at least 1 px) [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Files; docs/specs/files.md]

pickerGlyphColumns.source: estimate: Customize Folder, symbol suggestions per row [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Files; docs/specs/files.md]

pickerCell.source: estimate: Customize Folder, side of one symbol suggestion [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Files; docs/specs/files.md]

pickerPreviewSize.source: estimate: Customize Folder, preview icon edge [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Files; docs/specs/files.md]

iconSize.source: F1 gap 19: icons about 104 pt [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § App switcher; docs/specs/switcher.md]

pitch.source: F1 gap 19: icon pitch about 134 pt [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § App switcher; docs/specs/switcher.md]

selectionSize.source: F1 gap 19: selection square about 123 pt [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § App switcher; docs/specs/switcher.md]

selectionRadius.source: corner of the selection square: macOS 27's App Switcher measures 32.4-34.1 at the 45-degree point, concentric with its panel (60 less its 27.5-pt inset: switcher.padding and the pitch's margin round the 123 square); was 26, an estimate (ADR-0039 step 13, G5) [ref: docs/audits/design-polish-2026-10-29.md § 3.11 Radius roles]

panelRadius.source: the panel's corner: macOS 27's App Switcher measures 59.7 at the 45-degree point (512 Pixels release capture Finder-App-Switcher), concentric with its selection; was 30, the F1 value of the macOS 26 captures (ADR-0039 step 13, G5) [ref: docs/audits/design-polish-2026-10-29.md § 3.11 Radius roles]

padding.source: panel inner margin around the tile grid: macOS 27's App Switcher sets its first tile 21.5 in (its selection 29 from the panel's edge), so the selection square sits concentric in the 60 corner; was 14, an estimate (ADR-0039 step 13, G5) [ref: docs/audits/design-polish-2026-10-29.md § 3.11 Radius roles]

nameSize.source: estimate: app name under the selected icon [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § App switcher; docs/specs/switcher.md]

nameGap.source: estimate: tile grid to app name [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § App switcher; docs/specs/switcher.md]

nameHeight.source: estimate: app name line [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § App switcher; docs/specs/switcher.md]

edgeMargin.source: estimate: smallest gap between the panel and the screen sides; more apps wrap to a new row [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § App switcher; docs/specs/switcher.md]

showDelayMs.source: task (macOS model): the panel appears after this long with the modifier held, or at a second Tab; a quick press-release switches without it [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § App switcher; docs/specs/switcher.md]

layerWaitMs.source: estimate: the chosen app is activated when the compositor reports the switcher surface unmapped; if no such event arrives within this time it is activated anyway [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § App switcher; docs/specs/switcher.md]

fadeScale.source: estimate: panel scale at the start of the open animation (Reduce Motion: fade only) [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § App switcher; docs/specs/switcher.md]

crossfadeMs.source: ADR-0016: the fixed crossfade between two wallpapers of any kind (artwork, colour, picture; macOS: ASSUMPTION, check against design/reference); Reduce Motion makes it a plain switch

toolTimeoutMs.source: ADR-0016: a grassfield-wallpaper prepare that runs longer than this is killed (a 24 MP JPEG takes under a second)

listTimeoutMs.source: ADR-0016: a folder listing that runs longer than this is killed (a hung network mount never blocks the shell)

changeDebounceMs.source: ADR-0016: quiet time after the last settings change before a picture is prepared (a colour well dragged for a second makes one job)

cacheMaxBytes.source: ADR-0016 (owner answers): LRU cap of the prepared-picture cache, 512 MiB

maxListEntries.source: ADR-0016: pictures read from one folder

stateWriteMs.source: ADR-0016: quiet time before the carousel position is written to the state file

fetchTimeoutMs.source: ADR-0016 step 2: a grassfield-wallpaper fetch (three API requests and one picture, curl allows 60 s each) that runs longer than this is killed

onlineMaxWaitMs.source: ADR-0016 step 2: the online scheduler looks again at most this long after it went to sleep (the day's random slot lies within 6 h of 00:10 UTC)

onlineMeteredRecheckMs.source: ADR-0016 step 2: a metered connection is asked about again after this long

meteredTimeoutMs.source: ADR-0016 step 2: the nmcli metered query that runs longer than this is killed and counted as not metered (a hung NetworkManager never blocks the fetch)

lockStillMaxBytes.source: ADR-0016 section 6: the lock screen draws a wallpaper still only when it is a regular file of at most this many bytes under the wallpaper cache (a prepared JPEG at 4K is a few MB; a PNG of a centred or tiled picture is the largest case)

videoIdleSeconds.source: ADR-0016 section 5: a video wallpaper settles (rate eases to 0.25, then pauses) after this many idle seconds

videoSettleMs.source: ADR-0016 section 5: the playback rate eases from 1 to the settle rate over this long when the user goes idle (macOS: the video slows down and comes to rest)

videoSettleRate.source: ADR-0016 section 5: the playback rate a video eases down to before it pauses

videoStableMs.source: ADR-0016 section 5: the crash marker is cleared after this long of uninterrupted playback

videoMaxSeconds.source: ADR-0016 section 2: the longest video wallpaper (the helper refuses a longer one)

videoMaxBytes.source: ADR-0016 section 2: the largest transcoded video file (512 MiB)

videoToolTimeoutMs.source: ADR-0016 section 2: a grassfield-wallpaper transcode that runs longer than this is killed (the helper's own ffmpeg limit is 30 minutes)

aboutWidth.source: estimate: width of the About This Wallpaper card of the desktop menu (macOS shows a small panel of about this width) [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Desktop; docs/specs/desktop.md]

movingFrameMs.source: ADR-0040 IQ-W3 A (step 9): the moving Grassfield artwork advances on a timer of this period while it plays (the lock screen and the screen saver; the desktop draws it still, the integrator's review of e067f26f), never every frame (a cloud crossing a 1920 px sky in wallpaper.movingCloudMs moves under 1 px per step)

movingCloudMs.source: ADR-0040 IQ-W3 A (step 9): the time a cloud of speed 1 takes to cross the sky of the moving Grassfield artwork (slow, as clouds; estimate)

movingLightMs.source: ADR-0040 IQ-W3 A (step 9): the period over which the sun's glow of the moving Grassfield artwork brightens and softens ("the light changes slowly"; estimate)

movingLightDepth.source: ADR-0040 IQ-W3 A (step 9): how much of the glow's opacity the slow light change takes away at its softest (estimate)

movingCloudOpacityLight.source: ADR-0040 IQ-W3 A (step 9): the clouds' opacity over a sky of the light set (artwork.cloudLight)

movingCloudOpacityDark.source: ADR-0040 IQ-W3 A (step 9): the clouds' opacity over a sky of the dark set (artwork.cloudDark): faint, so the night stays dark

firstShowTimeoutMs.source: ADR-0040 section 6 (ID-3): the wallpaper window maps with its first frame (the output's last picture from the cache, else what the feed decides) at most this long after the shell starts or the output appears; then the artwork

phaseFadeMs.source: ADR-0040 section 6 (IQ-W1 C): the slow crossfade between two phases of the Grassfield artwork through the two-slot model; Reduce Motion cuts

phaseDawnBeforeSunriseMin.source: ADR-0040 section 2 (the time-of-day rule): Dawn starts this many minutes before sunrise

phaseDayAfterSunriseMin.source: ADR-0040 section 2 (the time-of-day rule): Day starts this many minutes after sunrise

phaseEveningBeforeSunsetMin.source: ADR-0040 section 2 (the time-of-day rule): Evening starts this many minutes before sunset

phaseNightAfterSunsetMin.source: ADR-0040 section 2 (the time-of-day rule): Night starts this many minutes after sunset

phaseFixedDawn.source: ADR-0040 section 2: Dawn's local time where the zone gives no point or the sun neither rises nor sets that day

phaseFixedDay.source: ADR-0040 section 2: Day's local time where the zone gives no point or the sun neither rises nor sets that day

phaseFixedEvening.source: ADR-0040 section 2: Evening's local time where the zone gives no point or the sun neither rises nor sets that day

phaseFixedNight.source: ADR-0040 section 2: Night's local time where the zone gives no point or the sun neither rises nor sets that day

cloudLight.source: ADR-0040 IQ-W3 A (step 9): the clouds of the moving Grassfield artwork in the light set, at wallpaper.movingCloudOpacityLight

cloudDark.source: ADR-0040 IQ-W3 A (step 9): the clouds of the moving Grassfield artwork in the dark set (a cool grey, the moonlit side), at wallpaper.movingCloudOpacityDark

settingsWaitMs.source: ADR-0040 section 6 (ID-5): no surface of the entrance shows before the settings are read (Settings.loaded), at most this long after the shell starts; then the defaults

revealTimeoutMs.source: ADR-0040 section 6 (P-6, ID-20): the longest the menu bar, the Dock and the desktop icons wait for each other and for the wallpaper's first frame at the session's entrance (shell/services/Entrance.qml)

revealMs.source: ADR-0040 section 6 (ID-20; ASSUMPTION for macOS, no capture): the one fade in which the menu bar, the Dock and the desktop icons appear together at the session's entrance; Reduce Motion caps it (Appearance.duration)

exitCountdownSeconds.source: ADR-0040 ID-21 (section 5): Log Out, Restart and Shut Down proceed by themselves when their confirmation is left alone this many seconds, as macOS's (“… automatically in 60 seconds”, ASSUMPTION from memory)

exitFadeMs.source: ADR-0040 section 6 (ID-10): the exit cover's one fade of the whole screen to the ground once the windows have closed; an estimate until P3 (Reduce Motion: motion.reducedMax)

exitWaitMs.source: ADR-0040 section 6 (ID-10): the longest packaging/bin/grassfield-session-end waits for the shell's exit cover, the ask included, before it ends the session (P-6 bounded waits; tests/shell/session_end.sh holds the helper's own bound to it)

exitCoverHoldMs.source: estimate: the exit cover lifts by itself when the session is still there this long after it came up (the helper that asked was killed before ending the session), so an exit that did not happen never leaves an opaque screen over the desktop (ADR-0040 ID-10, P-6 bounded waits)

ground.source: ADR-0040 ID-2 (P-1 one ground): the default artwork's ground (Artwork.ground of the dark Grassfield evening, held equal by tests/unit/tst_artwork.qml), the session's Hyprland background_color of config/hypr/grassfield/looknfeel.lua (held equal by tests/unit/tst_sessionexit.qml); the shell replaces it with the shown wallpaper's (shell/services/Ground.qml) and falls back to it

lightGap.source: ADR-0015 / f1-reference-gaps.md:103: gap between two light edges (pitch 23); plugin kButtonSpacing

titlebarLightInset.source: ADR-0015: titlebar style, left edge to the first light's edge (plugin kButtonInsetLeft); the centre is then at (16, 16)

lightHitSlop.source: plugin kButtonHitSlop = diameter / 6: extra hit radius around a light, the gaps between lights stay drag area [ref: ADR-0015; docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Window chrome; docs/specs/compositor.md § Plugin work item: client chrome]

inactiveLightLight.source: plugin titlebarPalette(Light).inactiveLight: grey light of an inactive window, light appearance; warm since the owner's warm neutrals of 2026-10-30 (ADR-0040): #D1D1D3 at OKLCH hue 85, chroma 0.0075, its lightness kept, so its contrasts stay [ref: ADR-0015; docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Window chrome; docs/specs/compositor.md § Plugin work item: client chrome]

pressedOpacity.source: estimate: a pressed light darkens by this much

titleSize.source: ADR-0015 / f1-reference-gaps.md:109: toolbar window title, about 15 pt bold

itemsGap.source: estimate: gap between toolbar items and groups

sidebarPanelInset.source: the floating sidebar panel's distance from the window's left, top and bottom edges, and the gutter between it and the content: macOS 26 System Settings panel at x 16, y 16, bottom 1785 of 1801 px at 2 px/pt = 8 pt (ss-004-005, measured 2026-11-03; Finder 8-9 px at 1.07) [ref: ADR-0024 amendment 2026-11-03]

sidebarPanelRadius.source: the floating sidebar panel's corner (a circle), concentric with the window's: the window's corner measures 16.7 pt circle-equivalent at 45 degrees (Hyprland rounding 17 at power 2.6, ADR-0024 note 2026-11-04), less the 8-pt inset (16.7 - 8); SidebarPanel draws it on whole device pixels (11 px at 1.25, 9 at 1, 17 at 2), so the panel's curve runs parallel to the window's; macOS 26 drew 18 to 19 in its 26-pt window (ss-004-005 at 2 px/pt, measured 2026-11-03) [ref: ADR-0024 amendment 2026-11-03 and note 2026-11-04; docs/audits/refinement-2026-11-02.md]

sidebarPanelRimOpacity.source: the light rim that lights the floating sidebar panel, 1 pt wide (2 px at 2x), snapped to whole device pixels: pure white (255) on the 249 panel in the light appearance, so the knob colour at full opacity (ss-004-005, measured 2026-11-03) [ref: ADR-0024 amendment 2026-11-03]

sidebarPanelRimOpacityDark.source: estimate: the same rim in the dark appearance, the knob colour at the toolbar's inner-rim 0.08 (no dark capture of the panel) [ref: ADR-0024 amendment 2026-11-03]

sidebarPanelRimWidth.source: the floating sidebar panel's rim, 1 pt: 2 px at 2x on ss-004-005 (x 16-17 and 444-445), drawn as a whole number of device pixels (1 px at 1.25) so its edge never splits between two pixels [ref: ADR-0024 amendment 2026-11-03]

sidebarPanelShadowOffsetY.source: the shadow sits a little lower than it is wide: 240 below the panel against 242 beside it (ss-004-005, measured 2026-11-03) [ref: ADR-0024 amendment 2026-11-03]

edgeDark.source: the window's contact edge in the dark appearance: macOS 27 draws one device pixel of near black outside the window (its light inner rim inside it is drawn by the compositor plugin, window.rimDark*, ADR-0024 note 2026-11-03); Hyprland's border colour, pushed by the shell with the appearance (C-4); the config's own (config/hypr/grassfield/looknfeel.lua); was the white rim at 0.15 (ADR-0024 note 2026-11-03) [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0024-visual-direction-27-structure-26-glass.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0039-design-polish.md step 6; tests/compositor/window_edge.sh]

edgeActiveOpacityLight.source: the active window's edge, light appearance: macOS 27 darkens the shadow under its contact pixel by 0.20 on every side (Settings General, Finder Home and Force Quit window crops, 2 px per pt), half a point; the same darkness per point in Hyprland's one-point border, one device pixel (0.8 pt) at 1.25: 0.2 x 0.5 / 0.8; was 0.25, twice that (ADR-0024 note 2026-11-03) [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0024-visual-direction-27-structure-26-glass.md; tests/compositor/window_edge.sh]

edgeInactiveOpacityLight.source: an inactive window's edge in the light appearance: 0.18 over its shadow (the inactive Settings window of the Finder App Switcher release capture), 0.18 x 0.5 / 0.8 [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0024-visual-direction-27-structure-26-glass.md; tests/compositor/window_edge.sh]

rimDarkWidth.source: the dark appearance's light inner rim, in points: macOS 27 draws 1 pt of white (two device pixels at 2 px per pt in the Appearance Dark release captures) just inside every window's edge, continuous round the corner arcs; the compositor plugin draws it over the window and its titlebar (CGrassfieldRim), in whole device pixels as Hyprland's border is (1 at 1 and 1.25, 2 at 1.5 and 2); none in the light appearance, none in full screen [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0024-visual-direction-27-structure-26-glass.md; tests/compositor/window_edge.sh]

rimDarkActiveOpacity.source: the rim's white per point, active window: macOS 27's Notes in the Appearance Dark release captures, window 41 and rim 62 over its two device pixels (white 0.10); the plugin draws the same light per point in its whole device pixels (0.125 in the one device pixel, 0.8 pt, at 1.25) [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0024-visual-direction-27-structure-26-glass.md; tests/compositor/window_edge.sh]

inactiveSelectionOpacityDark.source: estimate: the same, dark appearance (macOS's unemphasized dark selection, about #464646 on a #2B2B2B sidebar, white at 0.11; no dark macOS 27 inactive selection measured) (ADR-0039 step 17) [ref: docs/audits/design-polish-2026-10-29.md § 3.13 Inactive windows]

tileWidth.source: estimate: tile box the plugin fits a stage's windows into (macOS model: small live thumbnails in a left-edge strip)

tileHeight.source: estimate: tile box height (4:3), the plugin never enlarges a window past it

tileGap.source: estimate: space between two tiles (room for the stacked windows' 8 px steps)

edgeMargin.source: estimate: strip surface margin around the tiles, and gap below the menu bar

maxTiles.source: docs/specs/stages.md contract item 3: at most 8 tiles per strip

revealZone.source: estimate: width of the left-edge strip that reveals a hidden strip (menubar.revealZone model)

revealDwell.source: estimate: pointer rests at the edge this long (ms) before the strip comes back

hideGrace.source: estimate: pointer outside the revealed strip this long (ms) before it hides again

resendDebounceMs.source: estimate: geometry changes are sent to the plugin once after this quiet time; also lets the surface's input region reach the compositor before op:on

retryMs.source: estimate: op:on refused with no-strip (the surface was not mapped yet) is sent again after this long

retryMax.source: estimate: no-strip retries before the strip waits for the next change

badgeSize.source: estimate: frosted app icon badge at the bottom-left corner of a tile

badgeIconSize.source: estimate: app icon inside the badge

badgeInset.source: estimate: badge distance from the tile corner

ringWidth.source: estimate: hover and drop-target outline of a tile

ringRadius.source: estimate: outline radius, close to the window corner radius

ringGap.source: UI audit 2026-11-05 (LOW): the hover and drop-target ring sits outside the tile, this far clear of it, as the Overview's selection rings (overview.ringGap): one ring model for the Overview's windows and Desktops and for Stages [ref: docs/audits/ui-audit-2026-11-05.md]

dragThreshold.source: estimate: pointer travel (px) before a press on a tile becomes a drag

dragOpacity.source: estimate: opacity of the badge ghost following a dragged tile

releaseHoldMs.source: estimate (motion.fast): an Exclusive surface drops its keyboard first and stays mapped this long before it unmaps, so Hyprland sees the release while the surface still exists (a layer destroyed while Exclusive leaves no keyboard focus at all); the fade of Search and Apps runs in it [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0012-desktop-focus-model.md; docs/specs/desktop.md]

noticeRimWidth.source: estimate: the notice's hairline rim, so that it stands out from cards and tiles [ref: docs/audits/store-2026-10-27/parity.md]

noticeRimContrast.source: estimate: the rim at twice a separator's opacity (Appearance.separatorOpacity) [ref: docs/audits/store-2026-10-27/parity.md]

noticeIconSize.source: estimate: the offline notice's glyph [ref: docs/audits/store-2026-10-27/parity.md]

noticeBottom.source: estimate: the offline notice above the window's bottom [ref: docs/audits/store-2026-10-27/parity.md]

iconRadiusRatio.source: estimate: the generic icon's tile corner for its size (the app icon shape) [ref: docs/audits/store-2026-10-27/parity.md]

iconPlaceholderGlyphRatio.source: estimate: the generic icon's glyph for the tile's size, while an app's icon is missing or loading [ref: docs/audits/store-2026-10-27/parity.md]

searchMaxLength.source: estimate: the search field's longest query [ref: docs/audits/store-2026-10-27/parity.md]

settingsWidth.source: estimate: the Store's settings window [ref: docs/audits/store-2026-10-27/parity.md]

settingsMaxHeight.source: estimate: the Store's settings window at most [ref: docs/audits/store-2026-10-27/parity.md]

settingsMargin.source: estimate: the settings window's margin [ref: docs/audits/store-2026-10-27/parity.md]

settingsGroupGap.source: estimate: between the settings' groups [ref: docs/audits/store-2026-10-27/parity.md]

settingsLineGap.source: estimate: between a settings group's lines [ref: docs/audits/store-2026-10-27/parity.md]

veil.source: the light dimming slurp lays over the screen while the crosshair shows, and the fill of the boxes a click can pick (the same, so the veil is even; the box under the pointer takes the selection's fill and border), read by packaging/bin/grassfield-capture (ADR-0035 D-10, step 8); an estimate of the system's capture crosshair, which barely dims the screen; no measured value yet

frameVeil.source: the dimming of the display around the toolbar's selection frame (Capture Selected Portion, Record Selected Portion): black at 45 percent, as macOS 27 darkens the outside of the area visibly; clear on a dark wallpaper (the frame's hairline and the picture inside stay bright) and on a light one; the helper's crosshair keeps capture.veil [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]; estimate, no measured value yet

selection.source: the fill of the area being dragged, a light veil as the system's selection rectangle (ADR-0035 D-10, step 8); estimate

border.source: the outline of the area being dragged, a near-white hairline (ADR-0035 D-10, step 8); estimate

borderWidth.source: the outline's width in pixels, a hairline (ADR-0035 D-10, step 8)

toolbarHeight.source: estimate: the capture toolbar's floating bar (Shift-Super-5), one row of 32-pt buttons inside an 8-pt inset, as macOS 27's screenshot toolbar; its ends are round (a capsule of the macOS 26 glass); no measured value yet [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

toolbarPadding.source: estimate: the inset of the toolbar's buttons from its edge, so that a 32-pt capsule button sits concentric in the 48-pt capsule (radius 24 less the inset 8 is the button's 16) [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

toolbarButtonWidth.source: estimate: a mode button of the toolbar (Capture Entire Screen ... Record Selected Portion), wider than tall as macOS draws them, its selected state a capsule [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

toolbarButtonHeight.source: estimate: the toolbar's buttons (the modes, Close, Options) are 32 tall, capsules concentric with the bar [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

toolbarIconSize.source: estimate: the mode glyphs of the toolbar, a little larger than a window toolbar's 18 (control.toolIconSize): macOS 27 draws the capture modes' symbols large [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

toolbarButtonSpacing.source: estimate: the gap between two buttons of one group of the toolbar (the three capture modes, the two recording modes) [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

toolbarSeparatorGap.source: estimate: the room on each side of a separator between the toolbar's groups (Close | capture | record | Options and the action) [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

toolbarTextPadding.source: estimate: the side padding of the toolbar's Options button (its label and chevron) [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

toolbarChevronSize.source: estimate: the chevron after Options, the size of a pop-up button's chevron [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

toolbarChevronGap.source: estimate: the gap between Options and its chevron [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

toolbarBottomGap.source: estimate: the toolbar floats this far above the Dock's band (or the bottom edge of a display without the Dock), centred, as macOS places it over the Dock [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

toolbarCloseIconSize.source: estimate: the Close glyph of the toolbar, a cross in a circle at the left end [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

countdownSize.source: estimate: the timer's countdown, a square glass plate centred on what is captured (the display, the window or the area), as macOS shows the seconds left [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

countdownRadius.source: estimate: the countdown plate's corner, the alerts' radius (radius.alert) on a plate of that size [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

countdownTextSize.source: estimate: the seconds left, large digits on the countdown plate [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

frameMinSize.source: estimate: the smallest frame of the Selected Portion modes, each way (logical px): a drag or a handle never makes it thinner, so it stays a frame with handles [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

handleSize.source: estimate: a handle of the selection frame, a small disc at each corner and in the middle of each edge, in the frame's colour with a veil-coloured rim, as macOS 27 draws its eight handles [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

handleHitSize.source: estimate: the square a press takes a handle in, wider than the drawn disc so that it is easy to catch, as macOS's handles are [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

readoutTextSize.source: estimate: the size readout (W x H in pixels) next to the pointer while the frame is drawn, moved or resized, the caption size [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

readoutPaddingX.source: estimate: the readout's side padding on its small glass plate [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

readoutPaddingY.source: estimate: the readout's top and bottom padding [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

readoutRadius.source: estimate: the readout plate's corner, a small capsule-like plate [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

readoutOffset.source: estimate: the readout sits this far right of and below the pointer, as macOS shows the dimensions beside the crosshair [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

windowHighlightOpacity.source: estimate: Capture Selected Window lays the accent colour at this opacity over the window under the pointer, as macOS 27 tints the window it will capture [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

windowHighlightRadius.source: the window highlight's corner follows the window's own: Hyprland rounding 17 at power 2.6, measured 16.7 (ADR-0024 section 1, Window corners) [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

windowHighlightPower.source: the window highlight's corner is the window's own superellipse: Hyprland draws a corner of rounding x power / 2 points at decoration.rounding_power 2.6 (config/hypr/grassfield/looknfeel.lua), so a circular radius leaves notches at the title bar [ref: docs/specs/system-dialogs.md § Capture toolbar]

tabIndicatorWidth.source: the selected tab's indicator of GTK 3.24.52 Adwaita and GTK 4.24.1 Default (box-shadow inset 4 px): the generated GTK themes recolour it, never resize it [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0035-system-dialogs.md D-8]

barMax.source: own value: ongoing activities the menu bar shows at once, the most recently started (ADR-0052 D6) [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0052-ongoing-activities.md; docs/specs/menubar.md]

popoverWidth.source: estimate: an ongoing activity's popover under the menu bar, about Now Playing's two Quick Settings columns wide (ADR-0052 D6) [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0052-ongoing-activities.md; docs/specs/menubar.md]

appIconSize.source: own value: the publishing app's icon at the top of the popover (ADR-0052 D6) [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0052-ongoing-activities.md; docs/specs/menubar.md]

tickMs.source: own value: a timer's time in the menu bar and the popover moves once a second [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0052-ongoing-activities.md; docs/specs/menubar.md]

edge.source: the pointer within this many logical px of a free side edge tiles (grassfield-compositor kEdge before ADR-0036 step 1) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements; docs/specs/compositor.md § Functional requirements]

cornerBand.source: logical px at the top and bottom of a free side edge where a drag tiles a quarter (kCorner before ADR-0036 step 1; compared with the owner's captures in nested, F1) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements]

margin.source: logical px around and between tiled windows while Tiled windows have margins is on (macOS 8 ± 1) [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Window chrome; docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements]

centerMaxFraction.source: Center keeps the window's size, at most this fraction of the work area (kCenterMaxFraction before ADR-0036 step 1) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements]

previewDelay.source: estimate until measured in nested against the owner's captures: a drag's tiling preview shows after the pointer rests this long on a place (ms); Alt shows it at once (parity row M08: macOS shows a short delay, U) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Drags; docs/audits/tiling-2026-10-27/parity-matrix.md]

hoverDelay.source: estimate until measured in nested against the owner's captures: the pointer rests this long on the zoom light before the tiling popover opens (ms; about a second on macOS, parity row M19) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Popover and Window menu; docs/audits/tiling-2026-10-27/parity-matrix.md]

popoverWidth.source: the tiling popover's width (pt; owner's captures gs-068-161 and gs-069-175, parity row M19: 230 x 251) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Popover and Window menu; docs/audits/tiling-2026-10-27/parity-matrix.md]

popoverLightInset.source: estimate until measured in nested against the owner's captures: the zoom light's centre from the popover's left edge (pt; about 25 of 230 in public macOS 27 captures, never committed) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Popover and Window menu; docs/audits/tiling-2026-10-27/parity-matrix.md]

glyphWidth.source: a tiling glyph of the popover, the miniature screen's width (pt; parity row M19: 26-pt glyphs) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Popover and Window menu; docs/audits/tiling-2026-10-27/parity-matrix.md]

glyphHeight.source: estimate until measured in nested against the owner's captures: the miniature screen's height (pt; about 26 x 20 in public macOS 27 captures, never committed) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Popover and Window menu; docs/audits/tiling-2026-10-27/parity-matrix.md]

glyphPitch.source: between the centres of two glyphs of a popover row (pt; parity row M19: 52 pitch) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Popover and Window menu; docs/audits/tiling-2026-10-27/parity-matrix.md]

glyphStroke.source: estimate until measured: the miniature screen's outline at the popover size (pt; thinner glyphs scale it down, never under 1 px) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Popover and Window menu; docs/audits/tiling-2026-10-27/parity-matrix.md]

glyphInset.source: estimate until measured: the space between the outline and the zones inside it (pt, at the popover size) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Popover and Window menu; docs/audits/tiling-2026-10-27/parity-matrix.md]

glyphGap.source: estimate until measured: the space between two zones of an arrangement glyph (pt, at the popover size) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Popover and Window menu; docs/audits/tiling-2026-10-27/parity-matrix.md]

glyphRadius.source: estimate until measured: the miniature screen's corner radius (pt, at the popover size) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Popover and Window menu; docs/audits/tiling-2026-10-27/parity-matrix.md]

glyphOtherOpacity.source: the zones of an arrangement glyph other than the window's own (the window's own area dark, the others light: parity row M19) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Popover and Window menu; docs/audits/tiling-2026-10-27/parity-matrix.md]

glyphCenter.source: the Center glyph's window, in twelfths of the miniature screen, one zone [x, y, w, h] (a window smaller than the screen, in its middle) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Popover and Window menu; docs/audits/tiling-2026-10-27/parity-matrix.md]

glyphRowHeight.source: estimate until measured: a row of glyphs in the popover (pt; 251 pt in all for two headed rows, Full Screen and the separators, parity row M19) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Popover and Window menu; docs/audits/tiling-2026-10-27/parity-matrix.md]

layoutGlyphWidth.source: estimate until measured in nested: a layout of the popover's Layouts section, the miniature screen's width (pt; larger than the 26-pt glyphs so that each zone is a target, a four-column layout keeping zones about 9 pt wide; Windows also draws its snap layouts larger than icons, parity row W02; the height follows glyphHeight / glyphWidth) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements; docs/audits/tiling-2026-10-27/parity-matrix.md]

glyphNumberScale.source: own value: a zone's number, shown once the number keys picked its layout (TL26, TL27), over the zone's smaller side [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements; docs/audits/tiling-2026-10-27/parity-matrix.md]

suggestTileWidth.source: estimate until measured in nested: the widest tile of the suggestions (TL28; a live thumbnail with the app's icon and the window's title under it; Windows' Snap Assist, parity rows W04 and W12) (pt) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements; docs/audits/tiling-2026-10-27/parity-matrix.md]

suggestThumbAspect.source: own value: a suggestion thumbnail's box, width over height (16:10; the window is fitted inside it with its own aspect, TL28) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements; docs/audits/tiling-2026-10-27/parity-matrix.md]

suggestThumbRadius.source: a tiling suggestion's window thumbnail rounded as the Overview's (overview.thumbRadius 10); it was square (ADR-0039 step 13, G5) [ref: docs/audits/design-polish-2026-10-29.md § 3.11 Radius roles]

handleLength.source: estimate until measured in nested against the owner's captures: the middle of the stretch two windows of a tile group share along an edge where a drag resizes every window along it (pt; outside it the edge resizes one window, TL30; parity rows M43 and W18) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements; docs/audits/tiling-2026-10-27/parity-matrix.md]

handleBand.source: own value: the shared-edge handle is at least this wide across the edge (pt; the margin between tiled windows is 8; without margins the band takes half from each window, as Hyprland's border grab does, TL30) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements]

layoutLeftRight.source: Left & Right (macOS Arrange; also the halves of the Layouts section): the zones in twelfths of the work area, [x, y, w, h], the first zone for the window that asks (ADR-0036 Layout catalogue) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements]

layoutRightLeft.source: Right & Left (macOS Arrange): the zones in twelfths of the work area, [x, y, w, h], the first zone for the window that asks (ADR-0036 Layout catalogue) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements]

layoutTopBottom.source: Top & Bottom (macOS Arrange; the stacked halves of portrait outputs): the zones in twelfths of the work area, [x, y, w, h], the first zone for the window that asks (ADR-0036 Layout catalogue) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements]

layoutBottomTop.source: Bottom & Top (macOS Arrange): the zones in twelfths of the work area, [x, y, w, h], the first zone for the window that asks (ADR-0036 Layout catalogue) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements]

layoutQuarters.source: Quarters (macOS Arrange and the Layouts section): the zones in twelfths of the work area, [x, y, w, h], the first zone for the window that asks (ADR-0036 Layout catalogue) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements]

layoutLeftQuarters.source: Left & Quarters (macOS Fill & Arrange, Arrange with Option): the zones in twelfths of the work area, [x, y, w, h], the first zone for the window that asks (ADR-0036 Layout catalogue) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements]

layoutRightQuarters.source: Right & Quarters (macOS, with Option): the zones in twelfths of the work area, [x, y, w, h], the first zone for the window that asks (ADR-0036 Layout catalogue) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements]

layoutTopQuarters.source: Top & Quarters (macOS Arrange with Option; the 2 + 1 of portrait outputs): the zones in twelfths of the work area, [x, y, w, h], the first zone for the window that asks (ADR-0036 Layout catalogue) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements]

layoutBottomQuarters.source: Bottom & Quarters (macOS Arrange with Option): the zones in twelfths of the work area, [x, y, w, h], the first zone for the window that asks (ADR-0036 Layout catalogue) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements]

layoutWideLeft.source: two thirds and one third (Layouts section, owner decision T1f): the zones in twelfths of the work area, [x, y, w, h], the first zone for the window that asks (ADR-0036 Layout catalogue) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements]

layoutThirds.source: three equal columns (Layouts section of large outputs, T1f): the zones in twelfths of the work area, [x, y, w, h], the first zone for the window that asks (ADR-0036 Layout catalogue) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements]

layoutWideCenter.source: a quarter, a half and a quarter (Layouts section of large outputs, T1f): the zones in twelfths of the work area, [x, y, w, h], the first zone for the window that asks (ADR-0036 Layout catalogue) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements]

layoutFourColumns.source: four equal columns (Layouts section of ultra-wide outputs, T1f): the zones in twelfths of the work area, [x, y, w, h], the first zone for the window that asks (ADR-0036 Layout catalogue) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements]

layoutStackedThirds.source: three stacked rows (Layouts section of portrait outputs, T1f): the zones in twelfths of the work area, [x, y, w, h], the first zone for the window that asks (ADR-0036 Layout catalogue) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements]

classSmall.source: the Layouts section of an output under 1920 logical px wide (owner decision T1f) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements; ADR-0036]

classLarge.source: the Layouts section of an output 1920 logical px wide or more (T1f) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements; ADR-0036]

classUltraWide.source: the Layouts section of an output of aspect 21:9 or wider (T1f) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements; ADR-0036]

classPortrait.source: the Layouts section of an output taller than wide (T1f) [ref: docs/specs/tiling.md § Functional requirements; ADR-0036]

firstCheckMs.source: the first automatic check, 10 minutes after the shell starts (U7) [ref: docs/specs/updates.md § Functional requirements; ADR-0033]

intervalMs.source: then an automatic check every 6 hours (U7) [ref: docs/specs/updates.md § Functional requirements; ADR-0033]

paneFreshMs.source: the pane checks when it opens unless a check finished less than this ago (U8) [ref: docs/specs/updates.md § Functional requirements; ADR-0033]

checkTimeoutMs.source: the checker stops itself after 180 s and its children 5 s later; the shell kills it past this backstop (U1) [ref: docs/specs/updates.md § Functional requirements; ADR-0033]

waitTimeoutMs.source: the waiter blocks up to 7200 s on Omarchy's update lock, then checks for up to 180 s (U4) [ref: docs/specs/updates.md § Functional requirements; ADR-0033]

waitRetryMs.source: a waiter whose own answer is update-running again (its 2-hour wait ended with Omarchy's lock still held, or a dev fixture) starts the next one after this, never in a loop (U4) [ref: docs/specs/updates.md § Functional requirements; ADR-0033]

busyRetryMs.source: a busy answer (another run of the checker holds its lock) is tried again once after this (U4) [ref: docs/specs/updates.md § Functional requirements; ADR-0033]

recheckMs.source: an automatic check skipped while offline or metered is looked at again after this, or when the connectivity changes (U7) [ref: docs/specs/updates.md § Functional requirements; ADR-0033]

meteredTimeoutMs.source: the nmcli metered query; a hung answer counts as not metered, as the online wallpaper does (U7) [ref: docs/specs/updates.md § Functional requirements; ADR-0033]

minimumBatteryPercent.source: an automatic check waits while the computer runs on its battery at this charge or less (Luma's download condition: mains or above 30 %) (U7) [ref: docs/specs/updates.md § Functional requirements; ADR-0050]

launchCheckMs.source: estimate: after Update in Terminal… the pane asks for a check once Omarchy's terminal has taken its update lock, so the check waits for the update and the button stays disabled meanwhile (U11, U28) [ref: docs/specs/updates.md § Functional requirements; ADR-0033]

runPollMs.source: while Update Now runs, the pane reads the runner's state and the helper's progress this often; they are replaced by rename, never watched (U25) [ref: docs/specs/updates.md § Functional requirements; ADR-0033 s3.5]

runStartMs.source: estimate: after Update Now the pane says Waiting for permission… until the runner writes its state, at most this long, then shows the last run again (U25) [ref: docs/specs/updates.md § Functional requirements; ADR-0033 s3.5]

runClockSlackMs.source: a run whose state says it started up to this long before Update Now was clicked is that click's (the runner's clock is in whole seconds) (U25) [ref: docs/specs/updates.md § Functional requirements; ADR-0033 s3.5]

windowWidth.source: estimate: the window wide enough for the CPU tab's eight default columns (no macOS 27 capture measured yet; step 5 checks F1 against public captures) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

windowHeight.source: estimate: the window's default height (no macOS 27 capture measured yet; step 5 checks F1 against public captures) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

windowMinWidth.source: UI audit 2026-11-05 U5: the folded toolbar fits in English and French with a margin (lights 87, title room 120, actions 106, the resource pop-up 116 in French, the compact search 140, gaps and inset 32: 601 measured off-screen); was 600, the name and three columns as Files' minimum [ref: docs/specs/activity.md]

windowMinHeight.source: estimate: the toolbar and about ten rows, as Files' minimum (no macOS 27 capture measured yet; step 5 checks F1 against public captures) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

rowHeight.source: list row 20, as Files' list view (F1 gap 17: list row 20 +-0.5) [ref: docs/testing/f1-reference-gaps.md § Files; docs/specs/activity.md]

headerHeight.source: the list header, as Files' list view (files.listHeaderHeight, 28 since UI audit 2026-11-05 U38: the rows start on a whole device pixel at 1.25) [ref: docs/audits/ui-audit-2026-11-05.md; docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

chevronSize.source: the sort arrow in a header, as Files' list view [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/specs/files.md]

iconSize.source: the row's icon, 16 pt (spec AM10) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

nameColumnWidth.source: estimate: the Process Name column (no macOS 27 capture measured yet; step 5 checks F1 against public captures) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

columnWidth.source: estimate: a value column, wide enough for "0:01:23.45" and "123.4 MB" (no macOS 27 capture measured yet; step 5 checks F1 against public captures) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

commandColumnWidth.source: estimate: the Command column (no macOS 27 capture measured yet; step 5 checks F1 against public captures) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

columnMinWidth.source: own value: a column dragged narrower stops here, its header still readable [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

searchWidth.source: the toolbar's search field: Files' expanded capsule less 20, beside the five tabs [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

searchCompactWidth.source: UI audit 2026-11-05 U5: the search field while the five tabs are folded into their pop-up in a narrow window (macOS toolbars narrow the field before anything else goes), its placeholder still whole [ref: docs/specs/activity.md]

toolbarTitleMinWidth.source: UI audit 2026-11-05 U5: the room the title and its subtitle keep before the five tabs fold into a pop-up, as Files' toolbarTitleMinWidth [ref: docs/specs/activity.md]

rowAlternate.source: the alternate rows' fill opacity, as Files' list stripes (spec AM7) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/specs/files.md]

summaryHeight.source: estimate: the summary under the table holds four figure rows at the caption size and a graph under its title, as macOS's (no macOS 27 capture measured yet; step 5 checks F1 against public captures) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

graphWidth.source: estimate: one graph of the summary, a sample every pixel and a half at historySamples (no macOS 27 capture measured yet; step 5 checks F1 against public captures) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

figureWidth.source: estimate: a column of the summary's figures at most, a label and its value such as "Compressed: 1.23 GB" with room between (no macOS 27 capture measured yet; step 5 checks F1 against public captures) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

treeIndent.source: estimate: one level of All Processes, Hierarchically and of a GPU's group, the disclosure triangle and its gap, as an outline list (no macOS 27 capture measured yet; step 5 checks F1 against public captures) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

swatchSize.source: own value: the legend square beside a figure that a graph draws, in the graph's colour (AM7: the figures stay text at 4.5:1, the colour is the square's) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

historySamples.source: own value: the samples a graph shows, two minutes at Very Often and ten at Normally (AM29) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

inspectWidth.source: estimate: an Inspect window, the widest Statistics row ("Involuntary Context Switches:" and its count) with room for a path (no macOS 27 capture measured yet; step 5 checks F1 against public captures) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

inspectHeight.source: estimate: an Inspect window, its header, the tabs and the sixteen Statistics rows without scrolling when no value wraps (no macOS 27 capture measured yet; step 5 checks F1 against public captures) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

inspectMinWidth.source: estimate: an Inspect window's header and its three tabs on one line (no macOS 27 capture measured yet; step 5 checks F1 against public captures) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

inspectMinHeight.source: estimate: an Inspect window's header, the tabs, a few rows and the Quit button (no macOS 27 capture measured yet; step 5 checks F1 against public captures) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

inspectLabelWidth.source: own value: the labels' column of an Inspect window's rows at least; it widens to its longest label (French ones run longer), right-aligned against the values as macOS's inspectors [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

inspectValueMinWidth.source: own value: the room an Inspect window's labels always leave to the values (a path or a command wraps in it) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

appHistoryWidth.source: own value: App History (Windows 11's, AM67) shows its five columns without a scroll at this width; no macOS counterpart [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

appHistoryHeight.source: own value: App History's caption, its pop-up and about twelve rows [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

appHistoryMinWidth.source: own value: App History's name column and its four figures still readable [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

appHistoryMinHeight.source: own value: App History's caption, its pop-up and a few rows [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

appHistoryNameWidth.source: own value: App History's name column (icon and app name); the figures share the rest [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

performanceWidth.source: own value: the Performance window (Windows 11's, AM66) shows its sidebar, a large graph and two columns of figures without a scroll; no macOS counterpart [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

performanceHeight.source: own value: the Performance window's large graph, the composition bar and its figures [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

performanceMinWidth.source: own value: the sidebar and a readable graph [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

performanceMinHeight.source: own value: the sidebar's first rows, the graph and a few figures [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

performanceSidebarWidth.source: own value: a resource's small graph, its name, model and value on two lines [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

performanceSidebarGraphWidth.source: own value: a sidebar row's live graph (Windows 11's thumbnails are about this wide) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

performanceSidebarRowHeight.source: own value: a sidebar row's graph and its three lines of text [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

performanceGraphHeight.source: own value: the selected resource's large graph [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

performanceTileHeight.source: own value: one logical processor's small graph (CPU, Logical Processors; CPU History) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

performanceTileMinWidth.source: own value: the narrowest small graph; the grid fits as many per row as the width allows [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

performanceBarHeight.source: own value: Memory's composition bar [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

performanceFigureWidth.source: own value: the narrowest column of label and value pairs under the graph; as many columns as fit [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

cpuUsageBarWidth.source: estimate: a logical processor's bar in CPU Usage (AM71; macOS's narrow lit columns, no capture measured yet) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

cpuUsageBarHeight.source: estimate: CPU Usage's bars, twenty segments of 5 with their gaps [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

cpuUsageSegments.source: estimate: the lit segments of a CPU Usage bar (macOS draws segments, not a fill) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

cpuUsageGap.source: own value: between two CPU Usage bars [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

cpuUsageMinWidth.source: own value: CPU Usage's narrowest width, its title beside the window controls (a machine of few processors) [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

cpuHistoryWidth.source: estimate: CPU History (AM72), two columns of small graphs [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

cpuHistoryHeight.source: estimate: CPU History, about five rows of small graphs before a scroll [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

gpuHistoryWidth.source: estimate: GPU History (AM72), one graph per GPU [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

gpuHistoryHeight.source: estimate: GPU History, two GPUs' graphs [ref: docs/specs/activity.md; docs/decisions/ADR-0038-activity-monitor.md]

windowWidth.source: estimate: a new memo's width, the desktop notes app's default proportion (no macOS 27 capture measured) [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

windowHeight.source: estimate: a new memo's height, the desktop notes app's default proportion (no macOS 27 capture measured) [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

windowMinWidth.source: estimate: the narrowest memo, room for both boxes and a few words of the collapsed first line [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

windowMinHeight.source: estimate: the shortest expanded memo, the strip and two lines of text [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

windowMaxSide.source: estimate: the tallest memo, the store's own bound on a side (apps/memos/src/memostore.h kMaxSide) [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

stripHeight.source: estimate: the memo's title strip, thinner than a window titlebar as on macOS's desktop notes [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

boxSize.source: estimate: the side of the close box and the collapse box drawn in the strip [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

boxInset.source: estimate: the boxes' distance from the strip's left and right edges [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

boxStroke.source: estimate: the boxes' outline width, one point like the strip's own fine lines [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

boxOpacity.source: estimate: the boxes' and the collapsed line's ink, the memo ink at this opacity on the strip [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

gripSize.source: estimate: the resize grip in the memo's bottom-right corner, its three diagonal lines [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

gripLineGap.source: estimate: the gap between the resize grip's diagonal lines [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

textSize.source: estimate: the memo text's default size, the system body size of the apps [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

textSizeMin.source: estimate: Font > Smaller stops at this pixel size, still readable [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

textSizeMax.source: estimate: Font > Bigger stops at this pixel size, a headline on a large memo [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

textSizeStep.source: estimate: one Font > Bigger or Smaller step, one pixel as the system's font panel steps [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

textMargin.source: estimate: the text's inset from the memo's edges below the strip [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

collapsedTextSize.source: estimate: the first line shown in a collapsed memo's strip [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

cascadeStep.source: estimate: a new memo opens down and to the right of the front memo by this much (ADR-0051 D-5) [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

translucentOpacity.source: estimate: a Translucent memo's paper and strip opacity, the desktop showing through (ADR-0051 D-7) [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

ink.source: own value: the memo text, a warm near-black like the warm neutrals of ADR-0040; 4.5:1 or more on every paper and strip, tested in tests/visual/test_contrast_tokens.py [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

yellowPaper.source: own value: the yellow memo's paper, a pastel of Grassfield's own; dE 9 or more from the macOS colours of tests/visual/test_contrast_tokens.py [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

yellowStrip.source: own value: the yellow memo's title strip, its paper one step darker [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

bluePaper.source: own value: the blue memo's paper, a pastel of Grassfield's own; dE 9 or more from the macOS colours of tests/visual/test_contrast_tokens.py [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

blueStrip.source: own value: the blue memo's title strip, its paper one step darker [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

greenPaper.source: own value: the green memo's paper, a pastel of Grassfield's own; dE 9 or more from the macOS colours of tests/visual/test_contrast_tokens.py [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

greenStrip.source: own value: the green memo's title strip, its paper one step darker [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

pinkPaper.source: own value: the pink memo's paper, a pastel of Grassfield's own; dE 9 or more from the macOS colours of tests/visual/test_contrast_tokens.py [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

pinkStrip.source: own value: the pink memo's title strip, its paper one step darker [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

purplePaper.source: own value: the purple memo's paper, a pastel of Grassfield's own; dE 9 or more from the macOS colours of tests/visual/test_contrast_tokens.py [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

purpleStrip.source: own value: the purple memo's title strip, its paper one step darker [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

greyPaper.source: own value: the grey memo's paper, a pastel of Grassfield's own; dE 9 or more from the macOS colours of tests/visual/test_contrast_tokens.py [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

greyStrip.source: own value: the grey memo's title strip, its paper one step darker [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

alertFillOpacity.source: estimate: the in-memo Delete alert's veil over the memo, its paper at this opacity [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]

alertButtonFillOpacity.source: estimate: the in-memo Delete alert's Cancel button, the memo ink at this opacity on the paper (the paper is light in both appearances, so the system's button fill and label, white in the dark appearance, would be unreadable on it) [ref: docs/decisions/ADR-0051-memos.md; docs/specs/memos.md]
